In Continuous and Dynamic Batching, what failure mode triggers the following observed symptom?
"Edge case trigger: 'Root Cause'"

options.text: When adding or removing sequences from the active batch, position IDs or attention masks fail to account for differing sequence start offsets.
The scheduler's admission check only fires once the entire running batch is empty, so continuous batching quietly degrades into static wave-by-wave batching.
The tokenizer applies a different padding side (left vs. right) depending on whether a sequence is newly admitted or already in-flight.
Rotary position embeddings are computed relative to a sequence's index within the batch tensor rather than its own token offset, scrambling positions after a resize.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: When adding or removing sequences from the active batch, position IDs or attention masks fail to account for differing sequence start offsets.

Freeze the batch composition for the duration of the longest sequence's generation, only admitting new requests once it finishes.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: Use FlashAttention varlen (variable-length) kernels with cuseqlens prefix-sum arrays, avoiding flattened padded masks altogether.
